questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The tour will start on time by using unless to express the condition that would prevent it?
choices: Unless the museum will close early, the tour will start on time.
Unless museum closes early, the tour will start on time.
Unless the museum closes early the tour will start on time.
Unless the museum closes early, the tour will start on time.
questions.explanation: An unless-clause states the condition that would prevent the main outcome and is followed by a comma before the independent clause.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The supplies had not arrived by using a that-clause as the complement of the linking verb was?
choices: The reason for the delay was that the supplies had not arrived.
The reason for the delay was the supplies had not arrived.
The reason for the delay was because the supplies had not arrived.
The reason for the delay was that the supplies have not arrived.
questions.explanation: The that-clause states what the reason for the delay was, namely that the supplies had not arrived.
questions.skill: Expanding with a that-clause subject complement
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The students entered the laboratory with a fronted prepositional phrase while keeping the main clause unchanged?
choices: Before the demonstration began, the students entered the laboratory.
Before the demonstration began the students entered the laboratory.
Before the demonstration began, the students were entering the laboratory.
Before the demonstration began, the students entered in the laboratory.
questions.explanation: The introductory prepositional phrase Before the demonstration began is correctly separated from the main clause by a comma.
questions.skill: Fronted prepositional phrases and introductory punctuation
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The applications exceeded the available places by using the number of applications as the subject?
choices: The number of applications exceed the available places.
The number of applications exceeded the available places.
The number of application exceeded the available places.
The number of applicants exceeded the available places.
questions.explanation: In the phrase the number of applications, number is the singular head noun and therefore takes the singular verb exceeded.
questions.skill: Maintaining agreement with the number of
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The team left after the practice ended by using only to show that the team did not leave until practice had ended?
choices: The team only left after the practice ended.
Only the team left after the practice ended.
The team left only after the practice ended.
The team left after only the practice ended.
questions.explanation: Placing only immediately before after limits the timing expression and shows that the team did not leave before practice ended.
questions.skill: Placement of the focusing adverb only
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The teacher asked a question with an embedded interrogative clause in standard indirect-question word order?
choices: The teacher asked what the students had learned.
The teacher asked what had the students learned.
The teacher asked what did the students learn.
The teacher asked what did the students had learned.
questions.explanation: The embedded interrogative what the students had learned uses statement word order and correctly completes the reporting verb asked.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The student volunteered by adding a restrictive relative clause whose relative pronoun is the object of a preposition?
choices: The student to who the teacher gave a book volunteered.
The student to whom the teacher gave a book volunteered.
The student to whom the teacher gave a book, volunteered.
The student to whom the teacher gave book volunteered.
questions.explanation: Whom is the object of the preposition to, so the restrictive relative clause takes the objective form and takes no commas.
questions.skill: Using objective-case relative pronouns after prepositions
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The coach spoke about the defensive strategy by using a gerund phrase as the object of about?
choices: The coach spoke about to build a stronger defense.
The coach spoke about built a stronger defense.
The coach spoke about build a stronger defense.
The coach spoke about building a stronger defense.
questions.explanation: Using a gerund phrase after about makes building the verb form required by the preposition.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly joins these two independent clauses with a comma and a coordinating conjunction: The stage crew locked the doors. They turned off the lights.
choices: The stage crew locked the doors and they turned off the lights.
The stage crew locked the doors, they turned off the lights.
The stage crew locked the doors, and they turned off the lights.
The stage crew locked the doors and, they turned off the lights.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses a comma before the coordinating conjunction and correctly joins two complete independent clauses.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a relative pronoun in the object position of a restrictive clause?
choices: Ms. Ortiz is the architect who clients often contact.
Ms. Ortiz is the architect whose clients often contact.
Ms. Ortiz is the architect what clients often contact.
Ms. Ortiz is the architect whom clients often contact.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun whom is the object of contact and refers to the architect in the restrictive clause.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The substitute teacher organized the cleanup by using an it-cleft to emphasize the person responsible?
choices: It was the substitute teacher whom organized the cleanup.
It was the substitute teacher what organized the cleanup.
It was the substitute teacher whose organized the cleanup.
It was the substitute teacher who organized the cleanup.
questions.explanation: In an it-cleft, who serves as the subject of organized and identifies the person responsible for the cleanup.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly presents the counterfactual result of Elena's missing the earlier train by using a third conditional?
choices: If Elena would have caught the earlier train, she would not have arrived late for the interview.
If Elena caught the earlier train, she would not have arrived late for the interview.
If Elena had caught the earlier train, she would not have arrived late for the interview.
If Elena had caught the earlier train, she would not arrive late for the interview.
questions.explanation: A third conditional uses had in the if-clause and would have with a past participle in the result clause for an unrealized past outcome.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The visitors left by adding a fronted time clause?
choices: When the final bell rang the visitors left.
When final bell rang, the visitors left.
When the final bell rang, the visitors left.
When the final bell rang, visitors left.
questions.explanation: A fronted dependent time clause is followed by a comma before the independent clause the visitors left.
questions.skill: Fronted time clauses and comma placement
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The committee worked on the report by using a modal perfect to show that the committee failed to meet a past obligation?
choices: The committee should has filed the report by Friday.
The committee should have filed the report by Friday.
The committee should filed the report by Friday.
The committee should of filed the report by Friday.
questions.explanation: Should have plus the past participle filed expresses an obligation that existed in the past but was not fulfilled.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The runners reached the finish line with an introductory participial phrase while keeping reached the finish line as the main clause?
choices: Exhausted after the final sprint, the runners reached the finish line.
Exhausted after the final sprint, the finish line was reached by the runners.
Reaching the finish line after the final sprint, the runners were exhausted.
After the final sprint, the runners reached the finish line exhausted.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase exhausted after the final sprint logically modifies the runners while preserving the original main clause.
questions.skill: Adding and placing a participial phrase
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands Careful analysis is the next step by using an infinitive phrase as the subject?
choices: Analyzing the results carefully is the next step.
To analyze the results carefully is the next step.
To analyze the results carefully are the next step.
Carefully analyze the results is the next step.
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase To analyze the results carefully serves as the subject, so the singular verb is agrees with that phrase.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The landlord arranged for the roof to be repaired by using have plus an object and a past participle?
choices: The landlord had repaired the roof before the storm.
The landlord had the roof repair before the storm.
The landlord had the roof repaired before the storm.
The landlord had the roof repairing before the storm.
questions.explanation: The causative have construction places have before the object and past participle, showing that the landlord arranged for the roof to be repaired.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The candle flickered with a fronted since-clause that gives a reason?
choices: Since the window was open the candle flickered.
Since the window was open, and the candle flickered.
Since the window was open, the candle flickered.
Since the window was open, because the candle flickered.
questions.explanation: A fronted since-clause is followed by a comma and supplies the reason for the simple-past main clause.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The director thanked the intern by adding a participial phrase that modifies intern?
choices: The director thanked the intern completing the final report.
The director thanked the intern to complete the final report.
The director thanked the intern, completing the final report.
The director thanked the intern who completed the final report.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase completing the final report modifies the noun intern and therefore follows it directly.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a colon to introduce a list after The recipe calls for these ingredients?
choices: The recipe calls for these ingredients: flour, water, salt, yeast, and.
The recipe calls for these ingredients: flour, water, salt, and yeast.
The recipe calls for these ingredients: flour water salt and yeast.
The recipe calls for these ingredients: and flour, water, salt, and yeast.
questions.explanation: The colon introduces the list, and commas properly separate the four ingredients in the series.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The old stadium hosted thousands of fans by using used to for a past habit?
choices: The old stadium use to host thousands of fans.
The old stadium used to host thousands of fans.
The old stadium used to hosting thousands of fans.
The old stadium used to hosts thousands of fans.
questions.explanation: Used to is followed by the base verb host to describe a past habit that no longer continues.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence adds a fronted despite-phrase to The cyclists continued to express the obstacle they faced?
choices: Despite of the flooded road, the cyclists continued.
Despite the flooded road, however the cyclists continued.
Despite the flooded road the cyclists continued.
Despite the flooded road, the cyclists continued.
questions.explanation: Despite is followed by a noun phrase, and a comma sets off the introductory phrase before the main clause.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The finalist answered each question slowly by using a matching pair of em dashes to add a parenthetical description?
choices: The finalist—nervous before the interview, answered each question slowly.
The finalist—nervous before the interview—answered each question slowly.
The finalist, nervous before the interview—answered each question slowly.
The finalist—nervous before the interview answered each question slowly.
questions.explanation: A matching pair of em dashes sets off the nonessential description nervous before the interview from the rest of the sentence.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The printer and the scanner were not working by using neither...nor with standard subject-verb agreement?
choices: Neither the printer or the scanner was working.
Neither the printer nor the scanner was working.
Neither the printer nor the scanner were working.
Neither the printer nor the scanners was working.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the singular verb agrees with the nearer subject, scanner, so was is the correct choice.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The match continued by adding a dependent clause that expresses a contrast?
choices: Although the rain grew heavier the match continued.
Although the rain grew heavier, so the match continued.
Although the rain grew heavier, but the match continued.
Although the rain grew heavier, the match continued.
questions.explanation: Although introduces a dependent contrast clause, and a comma separates it from the independent clause that follows.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The student won the award by adding a restrictive relative clause that uses whose to show possession?
choices: The student whose essay impressed the judges won the award.
The student who essay impressed the judges won the award.
The student whose essay impressed the judges, won the award.
The student who's essay impressed the judges won the award.
questions.explanation: Whose functions as a possessive relative pronoun modifying essay, and the absence of a comma marks the information as essential.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The bundle was left on the workbench by describing its contents while preserving subject-verb agreement?
choices: The bundle of wooden dowels have been left on the workbench.
The bundle of wooden dowels are left on the workbench.
The bundle of wooden dowels was left on the workbench.
The bundle of wooden dowels were left on the workbench.
questions.explanation: The singular head noun bundle takes was even though the prepositional phrase names several dowels.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which expansion uses a correctly ordered that-clause with the past perfect to show the rules change before the coach's explanation?
choices: The coach explained that the rules have changed.
The coach explained the rules had changed.
The coach explained that the rules had changed.
The coach explained that had the rules changed.
questions.explanation: The past perfect had changed marks the change as completed before the coach's explanation, and the that-clause is correctly formed.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Given that Ms. Alvarez is the chemistry department chair, which sentence correctly expands Ms. Alvarez teaches chemistry by adding that information as a nonessential appositive?
choices: Ms. Alvarez, the chemistry department chair, teaches chemistry.
Ms. Alvarez, the chemistry department chair teaches chemistry.
Ms. Alvarez the chemistry department chair, teaches chemistry.
Ms. Alvarez, which is the chemistry department chair, teaches chemistry.
questions.explanation: The appositive the chemistry department chair is properly enclosed by commas and identifies Ms. Alvarez.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly states a conditional relationship with an introductory if-clause?
choices: If the roads were flooded the team bus would take a different route.
If, the roads were flooded, the team bus would take a different route.
If the roads were flooded; the team bus would take a different route.
If the roads were flooded, the team bus would take a different route.
questions.explanation: An introductory if-clause is a dependent clause and is followed by a comma before the independent clause.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence states the purpose of opening the window with an infinitive phrase?
choices: The student opened the window for hear the announcement.
The student opened the window to hear the announcement.
The student opened the window to hearing the announcement.
The student opened the window hearing the announcement.
questions.explanation: The infinitive to hear functions as a purpose phrase, explaining why the student opened the window.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The hikers rested by adding an absolute phrase that supplies information about the scene?
choices: The hikers rested beside a roaring waterfall, their clothes soaked from the spray.
The hikers rested beside a roaring waterfall, soaked from the spray.
The hikers rested beside a roaring waterfall, and their clothes were soaked from the spray.
The hikers rested beside a roaring waterfall, their soaked clothes from the spray.
questions.explanation: The absolute phrase their clothes soaked from the spray has its own subject and adds information to the main clause.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which version properly adds a nonrestrictive appositive to identify the coach?
choices: Coach Elena Ruiz, a former professional player teaches basketball skills.
Coach Elena Ruiz a former professional player, teaches basketball skills.
Coach Elena Ruiz, a former professional player, teaches basketball skills.
Coach Elena Ruiz, a former professional player; teaches basketball skills.
questions.explanation: A nonrestrictive appositive is enclosed by a pair of commas, so both commas around a former professional player are required.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains no dangling or misattached participial phrase?
choices: Checking the exam scores carefully, the researcher's notes filled three pages.
Checking the exam scores carefully, the researcher drew a firm conclusion.
Checking the exam scores carefully, the conclusion appeared convincing to the researcher.
Checking the exam scores carefully, the final decision was supported by the researcher.
questions.explanation: The introductory participial phrase Checking the exam scores carefully logically modifies the subject the researcher.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The city will plant ten thousand trees by using the future perfect to show completion before the end of next year?
choices: By the end of next year, the city has planted ten thousand trees.
By the end of next year, the city had planted ten thousand trees.
By the end of next year, the city will plant ten thousand trees.
By the end of next year, the city will have planted ten thousand trees.
questions.explanation: The future perfect will have planted shows that the planting will be completed before the future deadline.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly completes The librarian reminded the students by using an infinitive to state the requested action?
choices: The librarian reminded the students returning the borrowed books.
The librarian reminded the students to returned the borrowed books.
The librarian reminded the students for return the borrowed books.
The librarian reminded the students to return the borrowed books.
questions.explanation: The infinitive to return correctly supplies the action that the librarian requested from the students.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The club needs help with the event by using three parallel gerund phrases?
choices: The club needs recruiting volunteers, collecting donations, and organizing the event.
The club needs volunteers, donations, and organizing the event.
The club needs to recruit volunteers, to collect donations, and organizing the event.
The club needs recruiting volunteers, collecting donations, and to organize the event.
questions.explanation: The phrases recruiting volunteers, collecting donations, and organizing the event are three parallel gerund phrases.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The members elected Jordan by using a noun phrase as an object complement?
choices: The members elected Jordan for his role as team captain.
The members elected Jordan the team captain.
The members elected Jordan to be the team captain.
The members elected Jordan because she was the team captain.
questions.explanation: The noun phrase the team captain complements the direct object Jordan by stating the office Jordan was elected to.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The students volunteered and they also cleaned the hall by using not only...but also?
choices: Not only volunteered the students, but they also cleaned the hall.
Not only did the students volunteer, but also they cleaned the hall.
Not only did the students volunteer, but they also cleaned the hall.
Not only did the students volunteered, but they also cleaned the hall.
questions.explanation: Opening with Not only requires the inversion did the students volunteer, and but also introduces the second coordinated verb phrase.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence that adds nonessential information about the novel with correct relative-clause punctuation.
choices: The novel, which appeared decades earlier, inspired the film.
The novel, which appeared decades earlier inspired the film.
The novel which appeared decades earlier, inspired the film.
The novel, which appeared decades earlier; inspired the film.
questions.explanation: A nonrestrictive relative clause is enclosed by a pair of commas, indicating that the information about the novel is additional rather than identifying.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The skaters became more confident as they practiced more by using a past-tense the more...the more correlative construction?
choices: The more the skaters practiced, the more confident they become.
The more the skaters practiced, the more confident they became.
The more the skaters practiced, the more they became confident.
The more the skaters practiced, the more confident became they.
questions.explanation: The correlative phrases present both the increase in practice and the resulting increase in confidence in the past.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The playground needs repairs by placing a because-clause at the beginning?
choices: Because the climbing frame had cracked, the playground need repairs.
The playground needs repairs because the climbing frame had cracked.
Because the climbing frame had cracked, the playground needs repairs.
Although the climbing frame had cracked, the playground needs repairs.
questions.explanation: The introductory because-clause states the cause, and the main clause correctly pairs the singular subject playground with needs.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The discovery changed the schedule by using a what-clause as the subject and keeping changed in the past simple?
choices: What the volunteers learned about recycling was changed the schedule.
The volunteers learned what about recycling changed the schedule.
What the volunteers learned about recycling changed the schedule.
What the volunteers learned about recycling had changed the schedule.
questions.explanation: The what-clause what the volunteers learned about recycling functions as the subject of the simple-past verb changed.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The mechanic repaired the engine with a restrictive appositive that identifies the mechanic?
choices: The mechanic Priya repaired the engine.
The mechanic, Priya, repaired the engine.
The mechanic Priya, repaired the engine.
The mechanic, Priya repaired the engine.
questions.explanation: Priya follows mechanic without commas, so it functions as a restrictive appositive that identifies the particular mechanic.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The driver avoided the sharp curve with a gerund phrase serving as the object of avoided?
choices: The driver avoided to take the sharp curve.
The driver avoided take the sharp curve.
The driver avoided taken the sharp curve.
The driver avoided taking the sharp curve.
questions.explanation: A gerund phrase, taking the sharp curve, functions as the direct object of avoided.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The team arrived early by using an in order that-clause to express a past purpose?
choices: The team arrived early in order that everyone will hear the coach.
The team arrived early in order that everyone could heard the coach.
The team arrived early in order that everyone hearing the coach.
The team arrived early in order that everyone could hear the coach.
questions.explanation: In order that expresses purpose and normally takes a modal verb such as could before the subject and its verb.
questions.skill: Expressing past purpose with in order that-clauses
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The scholarship supports a student by adding a restrictive relative clause that identifies one particular student?
choices: The scholarship supports a student, who maintains a 3.5 grade-point average.
The scholarship supports a student which maintains a 3.5 grade-point average.
The scholarship supports a student who maintains a 3.5 grade-point average.
The scholarship supports a student whom maintains a 3.5 grade-point average.
questions.explanation: The restrictive relative clause who maintains a 3.5 grade-point average narrows the reference to a particular student and correctly takes no comma.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands Waiting for the results by using a gerund phrase as the subject?
choices: To wait for the results requires patience.
Waiting for the results requires patience.
Waiting for the results require patience.
The waiting for the results require patience.
questions.explanation: The gerund phrase Waiting for the results functions as the subject, so the singular verb requires agrees with it.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The evidence was incomplete by adding a second independent clause joined with a semicolon?
choices: The evidence was incomplete; the final report had not yet arrived.
The evidence was incomplete, the final report had not yet arrived.
The evidence was incomplete; because the final report had not yet arrived.
The evidence was incomplete and; the final report had not yet arrived.
questions.explanation: The semicolon correctly joins two complete independent clauses that express closely related ideas.
questions.skill: Joining independent clauses with a semicolon
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expands The visitors received directions by using each of the visitors as the subject, keeping the original active verb and preserving singular agreement?
choices: Each of the visitors were receiving directions.
Each of the visitors was given directions.
Each of the visitors receive directions.
Each of the visitors received directions.
questions.explanation: Each is the singular subject, and received preserves the original active construction despite the intervening prepositional phrase.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review
